problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=2y(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=-2x(t),\end{aligned}\,[\begin{aligned}x(0) \\ y(0)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]
$$

Find the solution to the initial value problem above.

*Hint: ${e}^{At}=[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t) & \operatorname{sin}⁡(2t) \\ -\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t) & \operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}],$ where $A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ -2 & 0\end{aligned}].$*

| $[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}]=\,\,$ |  | {{field-1}} |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | {{field-2}} |  |  |
worked_solution:
Writing our system in matrix form, we get

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ -2 & 0\end{aligned}]x(t),
$$

where $x(t)=[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}].$ So, the matrix of the system is $A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ -2 & 0\end{aligned}].$

Given the system ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t),$ where $A$ is a constant square matrix, the solution of the initial value problem can be written as

$$
x(t)={Φ}_{0}(t)\,x(0),
$$

where ${Φ}_{0}(t)={e}^{At}$ is the standard fundamental matrix of the system, and $x(0)$ is the initial condition vector.

Now, using the given information, the standard fundamental matrix ${Φ}_{0}(t)$ of the system is given by

$$
{Φ}_{0}(t)={e}^{At}=[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t) & \operatorname{sin}⁡(2t) \\ -\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t) & \operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, the solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & ={e}^{At}\,x(0) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t) & \operatorname{sin}⁡(2t) \\ -\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t) & \operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)-\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t) \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)+2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
